evidence.reason: The finding proposes new protection, not a fix to existing intended behavior. prepare-host.py is an operator-run deployment render script (docstring lines 2-5: 'Recorded, policy-free host rendering... The overlay and deploy records must live outside Git. See HOST-DEPLOY.md before using this on an approved deployment'), and the only placement guard in the code is the one the finding anchors on (still present at tip, apps/crq-python/ops/prepare-host.py:998, 'if not outside(output, root):'), whose purpose is to keep rendered artifacts out of the Git checkout. No supplied evidence — docstring, contract, or HOST-DEPLOY excerpt — states an invariant that resolved writes must be contained inside the preview root. The alleged harm requires the operator's own chosen output tree on an owner-approved deploy host (contract item 22 and the #395 'owner deploy-trust sign-off' posture) to already contain a symlink pointing at the live systemd directory; even the proposed child-containment check would not stop --output itself resolving to the live directory, showing this is a policy/hardening question about where the operator points the tool, not an implementation error in existing behavior. Adding resolved-path containment validation is an enlargement of protection scope, and an opportunity to harden an operator-controlled deploy tool does not itself establish a defect. The anchor code persists at the tip (line 998) and no commit in history implements the requested check, so it is neither fixed nor superseded; it is simply not a current obligation.
